findings: The November 7 capture turns the canonical URL into a Link with Web Elements overview for one-click custom checkout. It explicitly names saving payment and shipping information for new Link customers, recommended Payment Element triggering on selection of a supported payment method, recommended Express Checkout Element showing Link alongside Apple Pay, Google Pay and PayPal, Contact Details Element email authentication, deprecated Payment Request Button migration to Express Checkout Element, and the Card Element save/autofill route (new raw lines 5-21).

The May 8 capture covers the standalone Link Authentication Element. Pass a known email directly to the Payment Element when appropriate. For new users the sign-up prompt follows selection of a supported credit card, debit card or US bank account. A returning user receives a phone OTP, after which successful authentication permits saved payment and address autofill. The guide requires domain registration, uses a PaymentIntent client secret, makes the Address Element optional for shipping, and documents optional email prefill and email change events (old raw lines 6-50 and 54-128).

The mapped source lines 13-44 captures most of the May behaviors but needs historical and API scope, the omitted known-email alternative, the correct React identifiers, and a November overview. Capturing or autofilling contact data, displaying a wallet, or authenticating a Link customer is distinct from confirming, capturing or settling a payment.

The route targets and supported-method phrasing carry integration-selection guidance even where their implementation bodies sit elsewhere.

Contact Details Element replaces the historical component name in the overview. Dated May 27 evidence attributes the name change and continued JavaScript alias support to the Dahlia changelog. The November page provides no evidence of a new cutoff or a behavior change. The more detailed Contact Details guide separately preserves domain registration, standard Elements client-secret setup, optional Address Element ordering, one-render multi-step guidance and an onChange email event.

contributions.original_prompts:
New raw: `raw/stripe-payments-link-elements-link-2026-11-07.md`. Prior raw: `raw/stripe-elements-link-2025.md`. Current summaries: `wiki/sources/source-stripe-elements-link.md`.

- Q1: For `https://docs.stripe.com/payments/link/elements-link`, what central documented behavior, prerequisites, identities and state boundaries does the complete new capture establish, and how does it compare with the matched old capture and every mapped current summary?

- Q2: Which changes are substantive versus presentational or navigation-only? Which historical claims must remain dated, which conflicts need reciprocal warnings, and which API, UI, version, client/server or outcome qualifications prevent unsupported inferences?

reviewed_answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/link/elements-link, November describes one-click Link checkout in Web Elements, where new Link customers can save payment and shipping information. It recommends triggering Link on selection of a supported method in Payment Element or showing Link in Express Checkout Element beside Apple Pay, Google Pay and PayPal. Contact Details Element uses an email field to authenticate Link customers. Payment Request Button is deprecated, with existing Link integrations directed to Express Checkout Element, and Card Element remains a save and autofill route (new raw lines 5-21). The May 8 guide documents a standalone PaymentIntent Link Authentication Element using a client secret and a registered domain, with optional prefilled email and an optional Address Element between the authentication and payment components. Customers without a Link account can be offered sign-up after choosing a supported credit card, debit card or US bank account. Stripe displays a returning customer's Link-saved addresses and methods after successful authentication with a one-time code sent to their phone. May also recommends passing already-known email directly to Payment Element (old raw lines 6-12, old raw lines 19-50 and old raw lines 54-128). The mapped source-stripe-elements-link.md lines 13-22 retain the sign-up and phone-code behavior but omit that known-email alternative. Its lines 34-44 reproduce the old lowercase React JSX, and the source does not yet cover November's scope. Client authentication and autofill establish no payment confirmation, capture or settlement.
reviewed_answers.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/link/elements-link, replacing the full how-to with links is structural, while the preferred routes, their trigger and display behavior, the renamed authentication route and the Payment Request Button migration affect integration decisions (new raw lines 9-21). In source-stripe-elements-link.md preserve the dated setup, sign-up and successful phone-OTP conditions, registered domain, optional shipping placement, email prefill, single rendering and change handler (old raw lines 6-50 and old raw lines 54-128). Link May guidance and November routes reciprocally. The May 27 Dahlia rename preserves behavior and both standard Stripe.js creation strings, `linkAuthentication` and `contactDetails`, with existing integrations requiring no change (raw/stripe-changelog-dahlia-2026-05-27-link-authentication-element-rename-2026-11-07.md:5-13). The legacy lowercase `<linkAuthenticationElement>` JSX is the example discrepancy. The retained @stripe/react-stripe-js 7.0.0 standard root exports `LinkAuthenticationElement` and `ContactDetailsElement`, mapped to their corresponding Stripe.js strings, and `LinkSignupElement` is a separate beta (raw/github/stripe/react-stripe-js/snapshots/2026-10-16-3b42f3d/files/package.json:1-11 and raw/github/stripe/react-stripe-js/snapshots/2026-10-16-3b42f3d/files/src/index.ts:102-119). Scope those root Elements and client-secret examples to standard PaymentIntent integration. The separate May 27 addition links to Checkout Sessions API version 2026-05-27.dahlia for Contact Details Element email collection, validation and Link sign-in, where Checkout Sessions previously required a custom email input with `updateEmail` (raw/stripe-changelog-dahlia-2026-05-27-add-contact-details-element-to-checkout-2026-11-07.md:5-15). The root exports do not define the Checkout entrypoint. The deprecation and recommended Express Checkout migration apply to Payment Request Button. The listed Card Element route retains its save and autofill purpose, with a separate guide preferring other Elements. The overview establishes neither runtime interoperability nor a completed payment.
